evidence.text: Positioning into the print: a 4.53% disclosed aggregate short, building +0.11pp in the last sessions (the baseline reads it as 0.0 through a name-join failure), sits against the Persson family's Ramsbury bid. The family has bought in size ON the report day of each of the last three prints: 2.0m shares on 2026-01-29, 4.5m on 2026-03-26 and 2.75m on 2026-06-25, each more than a normal day's volume. evidence.source_date: 2026-06-30 (publication of the 2026-06-25 trade); short register row dated 2026-09-22
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The family bought on report day in all three 2026 prints and the stock still closed down each time: -0.7% (Q4, 2026-01-29), -2.2% (Q1, 2026-03-26), -0.6% (Q2, 2026-06-25), per Modular's report-day table. The one squeeze in the recent record is Q3 2025, +9.8% on 2025-09-25, on a gross-margin beat. So the bid has cushioned downside and has not produced upside on its own.
evidence.why_not_priced: The sealed lean (+0.37) contains only the run-up: its short_squeeze component is 0.0 because the register join missed a 4.53% short. A fully priced squeeze would show up as a stock rallying into the print while the short covered. Instead the short is adding (+0.11pp since the 09-02 level) and the stock drifted 12% lower through the closed period with its largest buyer barred from the tape. The family pattern is public in the FI insider register and in Swedish press, so this is flow timing rather than hidden information, and it is sized small for that reason.
evidence.independence: The short level and the family buying come from two different FI registers: https://www.fi.se/sv/vara-register/blankningsregistret/GetBlankningsregisterAggregat/ and the insynsregister above. That the stock drifted without the bid is read off the Yahoo tape (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/HM-B.ST?range=3mo&interval=1d). No third source says the setup will squeeze.

evidence.text: A US IEEPA tariff refund of up to SEK 1.5bn (Citi) is likely to land in the Jun-Aug quarter's P&L and appears to be outside the published bar. H&M has said nothing about it on either 2026 call. CBP had paid out about $100bn by 31 July, and Pandora booked a partial refund in its Apr-Jun quarter as a 230bp one-off gross-margin item.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: H&M has no prior refund print. The closest analogue is Nordic peer Pandora: it booked the refund as a flagged one-off, raised margin guidance explicitly on it, and the stock fell 1.74% on underlying weakness (https://www.investing.com/news/company-news/pandora-raises-2026-guidance-on-tariff-refund-q2-growth-93CH-4855608, 2026-08-12). H&M's own last gross-margin beat (Q3 2025) was paid +9.8%, but that was operating margin, not a one-off.
evidence.why_not_priced: The bar looks like it excludes the refund. Consensus EBIT of SEK 5,095m is only +3.7% y/y, and consensus gross margin of 53.37% matches Citi's own ex-refund 53.3%. If the refund were in the bar, EBIT would be near SEK 6.1-6.6bn. The market already knows about it, though: Citi's note moved the stock +4.05% on 2026-08-18 and the gain has since been fully given back. On close-to-close the market will likely strip a flagged one-off, which is why this is [sizing note removed]. The lessons file's four US refund names split up or down by double digits on guidance direction, so the sign here really belongs to the September sales line, which nobody can see.
evidence.independence: Two different Swedish outlets carry the same Citi figure: https://efn.se/handms-akilleshal-i-fokus-infor-rapporten (2026-09-22) and https://www.privataaffarer.se/placeringar/aktier/citi-kladjatten-en-stor-vinnare-vid-tullaterbetalning/ (2026-03-06, 12% of FY EBIT). evidence.text: The EU 21st-package carve-out that drove DLNG from $3.32 (16 July) to $3.85 (23 July) is a third-country-deliveries-only derogation expiring 25 July 2027, renewable one year at a time by Council vote and capped at the operator's 2025 volumes; the AIS work identifying the Dynagas vessels it protects names Clean Planet, Clean Vision, Clean Ocean and Clean Horizon - none of which are among the listed partnership's six ships - while DLNG's own Yamal-chartered Lena River last called at Huelva, Spain, an EU import terminal, departing 25 August 2026, i.e. exactly the EU-delivery employment the derogation does not cover.
evidence.why_not_priced: Dynagas holds no earnings call and has said nothing in writing since 29 May 2026, when its 6-K still stated that losing the Yamal charters 'would have a material adverse effect' and that it was studying 'the feasibility of lawfully removing the E.U. nexus'; the 8 September release is the first company text after the derogation. If the market had read the derogation's terms rather than the headline it would not have paid +9.17% and +4.34% on 22-23 July and then held most of it - and a $135m MLP with no analyst coverage, no EPS estimate and 41 contracts of total option open interest has no mechanism through which anyone reconciled the Official Journal text with which four hulls actually sit inside the listed entity. Coverage, if this were priced, would look like a note distinguishing the sponsor's Arc7 fleet from the MLP's 1A fleet; no such note exists.
evidence.independence: Two separate documents reach the same reading of the text independently of the urgewald analysis: euobserver, 27 July 2026, states the exemption covers LNG 'to third countries' and explicitly not European deliveries (https://euobserver.com/230246/brussels-found-russias-lng-weak-spot-then-carved-out-an-exception-for-a-greek-billionaire/), and High North News, 4 August 2026, gives the 25 July 2027 expiry, the annual Council renewal and the 2025 volume cap (https://en.highnorthnews.com/politics/eu-softens-russian-lng-sanctions-allowing-shipping-and-trading-to-continue-beyond-2027/1115356). The fleet-identity leg is independently checkable against the partnership's own Q1 6-K, which lists its six vessels as Clean Energy, Ob River, Amur River, Arctic Aurora, Yenisei River and Lena River (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1578453/000131786126000029/f052926dlng6k.htm). NOTE ON CLUSTERING: the vessel-identity leg and the destination-split leg both come out of the same urgewald document, so treat them as one source, not two.

evidence.text: Clean Energy, the vessel DLNG moved onto a Rio Grande LNG charter 'at higher daily rates' at the end of April 2026, has sat at anchor in Southeast Asia in ballast (draught 8.9 m, speed 0.1 knots) with no destination and no ETA since departing Singapore Anchorage on 5 August 2026 - 33 days idle - while Arctic Aurora, still trading normally (loaded at Melkoya, Norway on 7 September for Klaipeda), is contracted to begin a second seven-year Rio Grande charter between September and November 2026, which would put a third of the six-ship fleet on hire to a project company whose Brownsville trains are not yet producing.
evidence.why_not_priced: Nobody aggregates AIS for a 50k-ADV MLP. This does not touch Q2 revenue - Q2 ended 30 June and time-charter hire is paid whether the ship moves or not - so the channel is the presentation's fleet-employment page and any disclosure of sublet or restructured arrangements with Rio Grande LNG, LLC, plus the Arctic Aurora delivery window. Had the market focused on it, a name whose entire equity story is charter counterparty quality would carry commentary on a pre-operational charterer holding two of six hulls; there is none, and the July rally treated the charter book as de-risked rather than concentrated. I am deliberately sizing this small because the contractual cash flow is unaffected.
evidence.independence: Two other vessels checked the same day on separate pages show the idling is not fleet-wide, which is what makes the Clean Energy datum interpretable rather than a data artefact: Ob River is en route Anjeong, Korea (departed 5 September) to Zhuhai, China (https://www.vesselfinder.com/vessels/details/9315692), and Arctic Aurora departed Melkoya, Norway on 7 September at 18.3 knots for Klaipeda (https://www.vesselfinder.com/vessels/details/9645970). Separately, the partnership's Q1 6-K is the source for the end-April Rio Grande delivery and the 'higher daily rates' characterisation (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1578453/000131786126000029/f052926dlng6k.htm).

evidence.text: Six directors of Dynagas LNG Partners filed initial Section 16 ownership statements on 18 and 30 March 2026, every one of them carrying event date 18 March 2026 - George Prokopiou reporting 15,595,000 common units and 35,526 GP units indirectly through Dynagas Holding Ltd (50.4% beneficial interest), Alexios Rodopoulos 500 units direct, Dimitrios Anagnostopoulos 'no securities owned' - even though the partnership is exempt from Section 16 as a foreign private issuer under Rule 3a12-3(b), filed a 20-F for FY2025 on 8 April 2026 and has continued filing 6-Ks rather than 10-Qs through 13 August 2026; no Form 4 has followed in the five and a half months since.
evidence.why_not_priced: I am filing this at zero because I could not resolve it, not because it is unimportant: it is a genuine contradiction in the filing record that I can document and cannot explain. A board that becomes Section 16 reporting normally means the issuer has concluded it no longer qualifies as a foreign private issuer, which would force 10-Q/10-K/8-K, US-GAAP-only reporting and proxy statements - or it is the compliance footprint of a transaction. Neither has surfaced. If the market had noticed, a $135m MLP would show speculation about domestic-filer conversion or a going-private, and the 8 September event would not be scheduled as a 6-K with no conference call. I refuse to guess a sign, so it carries no directional weight; the band is width, not a view.
evidence.independence: none - the only corroboration is that the same EDGAR submissions index shows both the Form 3 cluster and the continuing 6-K/20-F pattern, which is the same source (https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001578453.json), and no press, filing or company statement anywhere explains the 18 March 2026 event date.

Sponsor take-private or unit accumulation - no SC 13D and no SC 13D/A has been filed since 2017 and there has been no Form 4 ever. Herfort, for 1,901,981 units (5.17%), event date 4 August 2026, filed 11 August 2026 - real flow at ~38x average daily volume, but it is on EDGAR and was written up by aggregators, so I treat it as thinly priced rather than unpriced and give it no weight (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1578453/000119983526000285/xslSCHEDULE_13G_X02/primary_doc.xml).

Refinancing - the four sale-and-leaseback facilities with China Development Bank Financial Leasing (Clean Energy $38.6m, Ob River $51.2m, Amur River $52.7m ~3 years each, Arctic Aurora $125.2m ~9 years, $266.2m total) amortise rather than balloon, $11.0m repaid in Q1 2026, so there is no maturity wall for a refinancing announcement to clear.

evidence.text: The published quarterly consensus is not a forecast of the company that will report - $93.05m revenue is exactly MasterCraft's own standalone FY26 guide of $312m less the $218.967m it had already booked in nine months, and $0.622 EPS is exactly $1.65 less $1.03, while the company explicitly said that outlook 'does not include the pending combination with Marine Products' and then consolidated Chaparral and Robalo from 15 May, roughly 6.5 weeks of the quarter, at an MPX run-rate of $66.5m per quarter.

Short-squeeze setup: there is none. Short interest at the 2026-08-31 settlement was 81,961 shares, 0.1% of stock, 1.8 days to cover, down 63.9% from 227,041 on 15 August (https://www.dailypolitical.com/2026/09/13/innate-pharma-s-a-sponsored-adr-nasdaqipha-short-interest-update.html).
A hidden going-concern trigger independent of the Sobi closing -- the 14-Aug release already gives the pro-forma runway, so absent the closing condition there is no mechanical trigger.
Any new ATM, second tranche or additional capital-increase authorisation beyond the 17,647,059-share placement; nothing found in Innate's regulated-information releases after 2026-08-14.
PACIFIC-9 topline having already leaked or been released -- it has not; no AstraZeneca release exists.

A pipeline-decision or impairment angle: the pipeline prioritisation and the plan de sauvegarde de l'emploi were validated by the DREETS in December 2025 with layoffs completing April 2026, so the restructuring charge is old news, not an H1 surprise.
Hiring-page and LinkedIn signal for Phase 3 build-out -- Innate's careers listings could not be reliably dated, so I dropped the angle rather than guess.
Insider Form 4 / AMF dirigeants transaction clusters since the August placement -- nothing found, though I did not exhaust AMF's filing database.

Historical earnings reaction history: I could not retrieve IPHA closes around the real H1-2025 (2025-09-16/17) or FY-2025 (2026-03-25/26) prints from any reachable source, so I have NO genuine earnings base rate for this name and sized off realised vol (50.9% annualised, ~3.2% daily sigma) and information content instead.
